primitives.name: Fall-on-Ball Kinematics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Always fall on it or someone else will do so.
primitives.assumptions: Player trajectory is deterministic; collision is inelastic; body acts as rigid absorber.

layer2.mapping: State transition function F(t,v) → {secure, lose} based on velocity threshold and timing.
layer2.telemetry: Impact force magnitude and deceleration profile during fall.

primitives.name: Opponent Interference Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: If an opponent is about to fall on the ball it is sometimes possible to push him so that he will miss it, and the oval can then be secured for your side.
primitives.assumptions: Opponent motion is linear; external force is instantaneous and localized.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a two-player zero-sum game where interference modifies payoff matrix.
layer2.telemetry: Change in opponent trajectory vector post-push.

primitives.name: Ball Pocketing Mechanics
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the ball is moving, the legs and body together with the hands and arms can be used to pocket it up.
primitives.assumptions: Conservation of momentum applies; contact is elastic.

layer2.mapping: Kinematic overlap function P(v_{\text{ball}}, v_{\text{player}}, \theta) → {success, failure}.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation and relative velocity at contact point.
